chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Salih ibn Uqba from Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a group of people passed by on camels. He asked, 'Where are these men going?' I said, 'To the graves of the martyrs.' He asked, 'What prevents them from visiting the grave of the foreign martyr?' A man from the people of Iraq said to him, 'And his visitation is obligatory.' He said, 'His visitation is better than one Hajj and one Umrah, and two Hajjs and two Umrahs, until he counted twenty Hajjs and twenty Umrahs. Then he said, 'Accepted and blessed.'

He said, 'By Allah, I did not stand up [to leave] until a man came to him and said, 'I have performed nineteen Hajjs. Pray to Allah that He grants me the completion of the twenty.' He asked, 'Have you visited the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'His visitation is better than twenty Hajjs.'

key_terms.الشَّهِید الْغَرِیب: The foreign martyr (referring to Imam al-Husayn)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of visiting Imam Husayn's grave compared to Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elevates the Ziyarat of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) from a recommended act to one of supreme merit, declaring it superior to twenty accepted Hajjs and Umrahs. The dialogue with the Iraqi companion illustrates the concept of 'Kaffarah' (expiation) and spiritual completion, where the singular devotion to the 'Foreign Martyr' outweighs the cumulative ritual efforts of a lifetime. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the unique ontological status of the Ahl al-Bayt, where their graves serve as focal points for divine grace that transcend standard jurisprudential obligations.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 41. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to us by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Muhammad b. al-Hassan from Muhammad b. Ismail from Salih b. ’Uqba from Yazid b. Abd al-Malik who said:
“All these Hajjs and Umrahs are accepted and blessed.”

The narrator says that before they stood up to leave, a person came and told Imam (a.s.), “I have performed nineteen Hajjs. Pray to Allah that I complete twenty.” Imam (a.s.) asked, “Have you performed the Ziyarat of the grave of Imam Husain (a.s.)?” He replied, “No” Imam (a.s.) told him, “This Ziyarat is better than twenty Hajjs.”
